newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Northern League launches tax revolt.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Northern League launches tax revolt.

text.p: Italy's Northern League party, calling for an "act of courage" from its supporters, launched a tax revolt on Tuesday to press its federalist ambitions.

The League, which last month declared "independence" for the would-be republic of Padania in northern Italy, said its anti-tax campaign would carry on until it had achieved seccession from the poorer south of Italy.

"The push for change cannot come from the palaces of Rome. People must understand that a minimum act of courage is needed," former interior minister and senior League parliamentarian, Roberto Maroni, told a news conference.

Maroni said that from next month, anyone in the north of Italy who was owed a tax rebate should withhold personal income tax dues. In addition, he called on all northerners to stop paying obligatory licence fees for state broadcaster RAI.
The third part of the revolt was aimed at recovering tax payers' money, which the League said was being squandered by Prime Minister Romano Prodi's government.

Among the state expenditure the League objected to was funds being injected into a loss-making southern bank, Banco di Napoli, and money earmarked for Rome to prepare the city for the "Holy Year" celebrations in 2000.

The League estimated that every tax payer in the north was contributing some 1.3 million lire ($851.9) a year to these schemes. "All the money the state owes should be repaid through every kind of tax," Maroni said.
He said the League would shortly distribute two million copies of a booklet to explain to supporters how to pursue the tax revolt.

The Northern League won an unexpected 10.7 percent of the vote in Italy's general election in April, tapping deep-seated frustration over high taxes and a perceived incompetent central bureaucracy. ($1=1526 Lire)
